turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had intermittent flank pain for about five months, and over the past two years I’ve had five urinary tract infections. I’m not having fever, nausea, or vomiting, and my urinary habits are mostly normal except during those infections.
Is the flank pain on one side or both sides, and does it travel anywhere else, like to your groin?

“It’s mostly on one side—though it comes and goes—and it doesn’t really travel to my groin. I don’t have fever, nausea, or vomiting with it, and my urinary habits are pretty normal aside from when I’m having a UTI.”
Have you ever noticed any blood in your urine, either when you have the pain or at any other time?
“Sometimes I do notice blood in my urine, and it seems to be more likely around when I’m having those UTI episodes, but I can’t say it’s always present.”

Patient: I haven’t had any imaging like an ultrasound or CT yet. My symptoms come and go, but I mostly just get treated when the UTIs flare up.

“It seems to happen unpredictably, but it’s more noticeable around the times I’m getting UTIs—though I don’t always have the pain every time the infection flares. It comes and goes rather than staying constant, and it doesn’t seem tied to meals or exercise.”

“It can switch between worse and better, but it’s usually on the same side. I haven’t noticed a clear link to meals or exercise, and it doesn’t consistently improve or worsen with anything I do.”
